sources.entry: waveSDR - macOS native desktop Software Defined Radio application using the RTL-SDR USB device.

summary.one_liner: waveSDR is an experimental, macOS-native desktop Software Defined Radio app that works with the RTL-SDR USB receiver.
summary.what_it_does: The README lists features including RTL-SDR hardware support, dynamic device detection, a spectrum analyzer, a spectrogram, and AM, narrow FM, and wide FM (mono only) demodulators. It also offers mixer tuning and swipe-to-tune. The author describes it as a learning platform for macOS app programming and DSP techniques. Recent notes say a build from macOS Sequoia crashes in a DispatchQueue call, and that a HackRF One driver and an FSK decoder are in progress. The README does not include install or build commands.
use_cases: receive AM and FM radio on a Mac
view a live radio spectrum or spectrogram
experiment with SDR and DSP techniques
stack: macOS native frameworks (Apple APIs including DispatchQueue)
librtlsdr (port to Swift in progress as RTLSDR.Swift)
notable: Native macOS desktop app, not a cross-platform wrapper
Spectrum analyzer and spectrogram views with swipe-to-tune
AM and FM demodulators, including narrow and wide FM
Author is working on a Swift port of librtlsdr and a HackRF One driver
caveats: README calls it purely experimental software with many code sections needing improvement
Recent notes say builds from macOS Sequoia crash in a DispatchQueue call, with no working build yet
Wide FM is mono only; the project has been on a long hiatus
keywords: receive fm radio with usb dongle
